Some new test files use predictable names that an implementer would also pick. This risks downstream naming collisions when the implementer's tests overwrite or conflict with yours.

Colliding files:
  - "tests/ptrconv/ptrconv_test.go" test file may cause test name collisions

Please rename these test files to include a random hash so an implementer cannot predict the path — for example: test_{name}_a3f9b2.py, {name}.4c8e1f.test.ts, {name}_9d2c7e_test.go. Do NOT use "shipd" or "datacurve" — those are banned.

If a flagged file's NAME is mandated by the toolchain (a package manifest like Forc.toml/Cargo.toml, or an entrypoint like src/lib.rs), randomize its parent DIRECTORY name instead — the collision then clears because the implementer cannot predict the directory.

Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 3

meaningful_differences: Submission modifies GopherJS’s compiler translation and JS prelude to preserve destination pointer type identity, nil semantics, and pointer equality across explicit and implicit pointer and unsafe.Pointer conversions; candidate changes Go utility functions to enforce bounded integer conversions, rounding/truncation rules, and recursive reflect-based container conversion.

Submission introduces and uses runtime helpers for pointer handling ($isNilPointer, $pointerConversion, $pointerToUnsafe) and alters translateConversion/translateImplicitConversion for pointer types; candidate extends mathutil ToInt/ToInt64/ToUint/ToUint64, TryStr* helpers, and reflects.ValueByType/prepareArg/SetValue with cycle detection, key-collision checks, and strict modes.

Submission focuses on pointer identity, nil mapping per target pointer type, and unsafe.Pointer zero semantics within compiled JavaScript; candidate focuses on numeric overflow/underflow checks, NaN/Inf rejection, string rounding behavior, and deep conversion of maps/slices/pointers via reflection in native Go.
perCandidate.one_liner: Both rework conversion logic to align runtime behavior with Go’s expectations, but one targets pointer/unsafe conversions in the GopherJS compiler/runtime while the other enforces numeric and reflective conversions with overflow and container recursion in a utility library.
perCandidate.reason: The two patches operate in different repositories and layers with different goals: the submission fixes pointer and unsafe conversions in GopherJS’s compiler/runtime to preserve type identity and nil semantics, while the candidate tightens numeric and reflective conversions in a utility library, adding bounds checking, rounding, and recursive container conversion. There is no shared modified surface or common API/behavior beyond the generic notion of 'conversion,' so they teach different debugging lessons and should co-exist.
perCandidate.submission_summary: Adjusts GopherJS compiler conversion logic and JS prelude to ensure pointer conversions (including via unsafe.Pointer) yield values of the destination pointer type, preserve nil semantics, and maintain pointer identity and equality. Adds runtime helpers and updates translateConversion/translateImplicitConversion to route all pointer conversions through consistent logic.

meaningful_differences: Different repositories and layers: the submission changes GopherJS compiler codegen and JS runtime helpers ($pointerConversion, $pointerToUnsafe) to implement Go’s pointer-conversion semantics globally; the candidate modifies a Go code generator (goverter) to introduce per-invocation pointer-graph state in generated converters.

Submission scope is broad: covers explicit and implicit conversions among all pointer types (basic types, arrays, pointers to pointers, structs) and unsafe.Pointer, affecting %T, reflection, type assertions, map keys, channel sends, etc.; candidate scope is narrow: only when a new PreservePointerIdentity flag is enabled, and only for pointer-to-struct conversions, preserving sharing/cycles during a single conversion call.

Submission ensures destination-type identity and consistent nil representations across pointer types, including mapping unsafe.Pointer zero to typed nils; candidate keeps public signatures but threads hidden state, prohibits certain methods, and does not alter language-level type identity or unsafe.Pointer semantics.

Submission’s identity coherence is achieved by proxy caching on pointer objects in the runtime; candidate achieves identity via per-method maps in a generated pointerState struct passed through recursive conversions.
perCandidate.one_liner: Both address pointer identity around conversions, but one fixes Go pointer-type semantics in the GopherJS compiler/runtime while the other adds an optional pointer-graph state to a code generator to preserve sharing/cycles during struct-pointer conversions.
perCandidate.reason: Despite both mentioning pointer identity, the modified surfaces and behaviors are unrelated: one is a language/runtime semantic fix in gopherjs for all pointer conversions (including unsafe.Pointer), while the other is an optional code-generation feature in goverter to maintain object graph sharing only for struct pointers per invocation. There is no shared purpose-matched API or file surface, and the scopes teach different lessons (runtime semantics vs generator stateful graph mapping).
perCandidate.submission_summary: Adjusts GopherJS’s conversion translation and runtime to ensure pointer conversions produce destination-typed pointers with correct nil handling and stable identity, adding $pointerConversion and $pointerToUnsafe and routing pointer cases in translateConversion/translateImplicitConversion through them.

meaningful_differences: Different repositories and domains: a Go-to-JS compiler (gopherjs) vs. a Go expression evaluator (gval).

Submission modifies the compiler’s conversion translation (translateConversion/translateImplicitConversion) and adds JS runtime helpers to preserve pointer type/identity and nil semantics, including unsafe.Pointer mapping; candidate changes reflection-based selection/method dispatch, argument handling, truthiness, equality, and operators across multiple files.

Submission’s behavior centers on explicit/implicit pointer-to-pointer and unsafe.Pointer conversions preserving destination type, identity, and nil equivalence; candidate focuses on dereferencing through pointers/interfaces during selection, safe nil handling (no panics), method resolution on values/pointers (including promoted/embedded), typed key conversion for maps/slices/arrays, equality and string rendering for named/pointer basic types, and function-call nil argument typing.

Submission’s scope includes pointers to arrays/structs and interface comparisons within compiled JS semantics; candidate’s scope includes selector parsing, “in” operator over slices/arrays, short-circuit ops (&&, ||, ??), date() argument typing, and wrapping function call errors with full names.
perCandidate.one_liner: Both address Go pointer/nil semantics, but one fixes a compiler’s pointer conversion behavior and JS runtime helpers while the other overhauls an expression evaluator’s reflection-based selection, method calls, operators, and nil handling.
perCandidate.reason: There is no purpose-matched surface overlap: the submission changes a compiler’s conversion translation and JS prelude to implement correct pointer conversion and unsafe.Pointer semantics, while the candidate revises a reflection-driven evaluator’s selection, method dispatch, equality, and operator semantics. Any similarity (pointers, nil) is generic category overlap, not the same behavioral change on the same surface. They teach different debugging lessons and should co-exist.
perCandidate.submission_summary: Adjusts gopherjs’s translation of pointer and unsafe.Pointer conversions and adds JS runtime helpers so converted pointers have the destination type, preserve identity across conversions, and map nil correctly (including unsafe.Pointer <-> typed pointer).

meaningful_differences: Different repositories and layers: the submission changes GopherJS’s compiler and runtime (prelude) to implement pointer conversion semantics; the candidate changes go-tools’ U1000 analyzer to infer field usage across conversions.

Submission’s behavior is observable at runtime (pointer identity, typed nils, conversions to/from unsafe.Pointer yield correct nil and equality); candidate’s behavior is static analysis metadata (which fields are considered used) with no runtime effect.

Submission introduces concrete runtime helpers ($pointerConversion, $pointerToUnsafe, $isNilPointer) and integrates them in translateConversion/translateImplicitConversion; candidate adds a new conversions pipeline (collectStructuralTypes, processConversions, conversionMembers/conversionFields) and unions field-usage sets across type-parameter constraints.

Submission addresses pointers to arrays, pointers to basic types, nil mapping, identity preservation and proxy reuse; candidate focuses on composing field-usage relationships across struct/pointer conversions, type parameters, constraints, and unsafe.Pointer without implementing conversion semantics.

There is no purpose-matched modified surface or shared API/behavior; any overlap is conceptual and boilerplate to the domain, not the same task.
perCandidate.submission_summary: Updates GopherJS’s translateConversion/translateImplicitConversion and prelude to ensure pointer conversions produce values of the destination pointer type, preserve identity, and correctly map nil, including to/from unsafe.Pointer, via new runtime helpers ($pointerConversion, $pointerToUnsafe, $isNilPointer).

meaningful_differences: Submission focuses on pointer conversions: preserving destination pointer type, nil mapping (including unsafe.Pointer), and pointer identity across conversions; introduces runtime helpers to canonicalize and proxy pointers.

Candidate focuses on evaluation order: ensuring left-to-right evaluation for calls/receives/assignments, correct short-circuiting, map/index/slice operand ordering, and single-evaluation of assignment-ops; introduces a new compiler pass and many ordering utilities.

Modified surfaces overlap only incidentally (both touch compiler/expressions.go) but for entirely different purposes: submission adds/rewires conversion logic; candidate inserts evaluation-order rewrites and hoisting guards throughout expression/statement translation.
perCandidate.one_liner: Both patches align GopherJS with Go semantics, but one fixes pointer conversion identity/nil behavior while the other enforces Go’s operand evaluation order across expressions, calls, and assignments.

The submission introduces pointer-conversion machinery and runtime support to maintain destination type, nil semantics, and identity; the candidate adds a comprehensive evaluation-order framework and rewrites expression/statement translation to honor Go’s left-to-right rules. There is no purpose-matched surface or shared behavior; overlapping files are touched for different goals, so these teach different debugging lessons.
